commands.name: create-image
commands.description:
Create an Image
This endpoint creates a JPEG file(along with PNG) with JSON data and your template

options.name: --template-id
options.description: Your template id, it can be obtained in the web console

options.name: --output-image-type
options.description: - Output image type(JPEG or PNG format), default to `all`. Options are `all`, `jpegOnly`,`pngOnly`.

options.name: --expiration
options.description:
- Expiration of the generated PDF in minutes(default to `0`, store permanently)
- Use `0` to store on cdn permanently
- Or use the range between `1` minute and `10080` minutes(7 days) to specify the expiration of the generated PDF

options.name: --cloud-storage
options.description: - Upload the generated PDFs/images to our storage CDN, default to `1`. If you have configured `Post Action` to upload the PDFs/Images to your own S3, please set it to `0`.

options.name: --generation-delay
options.description: Delay in milliseconds before PDF/image generation

options.name: --resize-images
options.description:
- Preprocess images or re-size images in the PDF, either `1`=true or `0`=false. Default to '0'
- If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the `resize_max_width`, `resize_max_height` in pixels.
- Images to be resized need to satisfy the following conditions:
- The images with the content-type `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg` or `image/png`
- The image URLs with the extension `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png`

options.name: --resize-max-width
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum width of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-max-height
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum height of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-format
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the format of the image. Either `jpeg` or `png`

options.name: --postaction-s3-filekey
options.description:
- This is to specify the file name for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2/Azure Storage)`.
- Please do not specify the file extension
- Please make sure the file name is unique
- You might use slash (/) as the folder delimiter
- It's default to transaction_ref

options.name: --postaction-s3-bucket
options.description: - This is to overwrite the AWS Bucket for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2 Storage)` or the container for `Post Action(Azure Storage)`.

options.name: --postaction-enabled
options.description:
- This setting enables the Post Actions.
- Acceptable values: `0` (disabled) or `1` (enabled; default).
- It is enabled by default. However, if you have enabled BYOS and do not upload the generated PDF/image of this request to your own storage, please set this to `0`.

options.name: --meta
options.description: - Specify an external reference ID for your own reference. It appears in the `list-objects` API.

options.name: --input
options.description: Load request JSON from a file path, '-' for stdin, or an inline JSON object/array string.

options.name: --request-json
options.description: Request body as JSON.

options.name: --request-file
options.description: Path to a JSON request file, or '-' for stdin.

commands.name: create-pdf
commands.description:
Create a PDF
This endpoint creates a PDF file with JSON data and your template. We support synchoronus and asynchronous PDF generation.

options.name: --template-id
options.description: Your template id, it can be obtained in the web console

options.name: --export-type
options.description:
- Either `file` or `json`(Default).
- The option `json` returns a JSON object, and the output PDF is stored on a CDN. Use this with the parameter `expiration`
- The option `file` returns binary data of the generated PDF(Secure and completely private) and the response HTTP header Content-Disposition is set to attachment.

options.name: --export-in-base64
options.description:
- If export_type = `file`, the PDF can be downloaded in binary or base64 format. The value is either `1` or `0`(Default).
- The export_in_base64 is set `0` is to download the PDF in binary
- The export_in_base64 is set `1` is to download the PDF in base64 format

options.name: --expiration
options.description:
- Expiration of the generated PDF in minutes(default to `0`, store permanently)
- Use `0` to store on cdn permanently
- Or use the range between `1` minute and `10080` minutes(7 days) to specify the expiration of the generated PDF

options.name: --output-html
options.description:
- Either `1` or `0`(Default).
- To enable output of html content, set the value to `1` and it will return in the JSON response as html_url field (as a URL)

options.name: --output-format
options.description:
Specifies the desired output format. Options are `pdf` (default), `html`, `png`, or `jpeg`.
- By default, a PDF is generated.
- To return HTML instead, set `output_format=html`; the response will include a `download_url` field pointing to the HTML.
- To produce an image, set `output_format=png` or `output_format=jpeg`.

options.name: --filename
options.description: - Default to UUID (e.g 0c93bd9e-9ebb-4634-a70f-de9131848416.pdf). Use this to specify custom file name, it should end with `.pdf`

options.name: --direct-download
options.description: - ContentDisposition set to attachment. 1=true, 0=false. Default to '0'

options.name: --cloud-storage
options.description: - Upload the generated PDFs/images to our storage CDN, default to `1`. If you have configured `Post Action` to upload the PDFs/Images to your own S3, please set it to `0`.

options.name: --load-data-from
options.description: Load JSON data from a remote URL instead of the request body. If load_data_from is specified, the JSON data in the request will be ignored.

options.name: --extract-link
options.description: - Extract links from the HTML content, default to `0`.

options.name: --generation-delay
options.description: Delay in milliseconds before PDF/image generation

options.name: --image-resample-res
options.description: - We embed the original images by default, meaning large PDF file sizes. Specifying the option 'image_resample_res' helps reduce the PDF file size by downsampling the images of the current PDF to a resolution(in DPI). Common values are 72, 96, 150, 300 and 600.

options.name: --resize-images
options.description:
- Preprocess images or re-size images in the PDF, either `1`=true or `0`=false. Default to '0'
- If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the `resize_max_width`, `resize_max_height` in pixels.
- Images to be resized need to satisfy the following conditions:
- The images with the content-type `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg` or `image/png`
- The image URLs with the extension `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png`

options.name: --resize-max-width
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum width of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-max-height
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum height of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-format
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the format of the image. Either `jpeg` or `png`

options.name: --postaction-s3-filekey
options.description:
- This is to specify the file name for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2/Azure Storage)`.
- Please do not specify the file extension
- Please make sure the file name is unique
- You might use slash (/) as the folder delimiter
- It's default to transaction_ref

options.name: --postaction-s3-bucket
options.description: - This is to overwrite the AWS Bucket for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2 Storage)` or the container for `Post Action(Azure Storage)`.

options.name: --postaction-enabled
options.description:
- This setting enables the Post Actions.
- Acceptable values: `0` (disabled) or `1` (enabled; default).
- It is enabled by default. However, if you have enabled BYOS and do not upload the generated PDF/image of this request to your own storage, please set this to `0`.

options.name: --meta
options.description: - Specify an external reference ID for your own reference. It appears in the `list-objects` API.

options.name: --async
options.description:
- Either `1` or `0`(Default).  `0` is synchronous call(default), `1` is asynchronous call
- To generate PDF asynchronously, set the value to `1` and the API call returns immediately. Once the PDF document is generated, we will make a HTTP/HTTPS GET to your URL(webhook_url) and will retry for 3 times before giving up.
- If `async` is set to `1`, then `webhook_url` is mandatory

options.name: --webhook-url
options.description:
- It is the URL of your webhook URL, it starts with http:// or https:// and has to be urlencoded.
- If `async` is set to `1`, then you have to specify the `webhook_url`.
#### Format of Webhook callback
Once the PDF is generated, we will initiate a HTTP/HTTPS GET call to the following URL:
https://`[yourwebserver.com]`?&primary_url=`[primary_url]`&transaction_ref=`[transaction_ref]`&status=`[status]`&message=`[message]`
- `[yourwebserver.com]`: The web services to handle the callback, which is the `webhook_url`
- `[primary_url]`: The URL to the PDF document
- `[transaction_ref]`: The transaction reference number
- `[status]` : Status of the transaction, either `success` or `error`
- `[message]` : Status message
***The following is a sample webhook call back to your server***
https://yourwebserver.com?&primary_url=https%3A%2F%2Fpub-cdn.apitemplate.io%2F2021%2F06%2Fb692183d-46d7-3213-891a-460a5814ad3f.pdf&transaction_ref=b692183d-46d7-3213-891a-460a5814ad3f&status=success

options.name: --webhook-method
options.description: - The HTTP method of the webhook, either `POST` or `GET`. Default to `GET`

options.name: --webhook-headers
options.description:
- The HTTP headers of the webhook, it should be a base64 encoded JSON object.
- The following is an example of base64 encoded JSON:
```json
eyJ3b3JrZmxvdy1hcGkta2V5Ijoia2V5X0VLc3MxNWJKRXFBMkRHYzM4bkNXNzlaRER1ZUZJeiJ9
```
The JSON object in clear text for the above base64 encoded JSON:
```json
{
"workflow-api-key": "key_EKss15bJEqA2DGc38nCW79ZDDueFIz"
}
```

options.name: --body
options.description: The HTML body content for the PDF. This property supports HTML markup and can include Jinja2 syntax (e.g {{name}}). The value of {{name}} will be replaced with the actual value provided in the data object.

options.name: --css
options.description: The CSS styles to be applied to the PDF. This property should contain valid CSS markup and should also include the style tag.

options.name: --data
options.description: The data object containing values for dynamic content in the HTML body. This object should include properties with corresponding values.

options.name: --settings-paper-size
options.description: Specifies the paper size for the PDF. The available options are Letter, Legal, Tabloid, Ledger, A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5,A6 or custom. custom dimensions specified as "custom_width" and "custom_height".

options.name: --settings-custom-width
options.description: Custom width for the custom paper size. Valid units are mm, px and cm. eg: 30mm

options.name: --settings-custom-height
options.description: Custom height for the custom paper size. Valid units are mm, px and cm. eg: 30mm

options.name: --settings-orientation
options.description: Specifies the orientation of the PDF. The available options are "1" for portrait and "2" for landscape.

options.name: --settings-header-font-size
options.description: Specifies the font size for the header in the PDF.

options.name: --settings-margin-top
options.description: Specify the top margin for the PDF in millimeters (mm).

options.name: --settings-margin-right
options.description: Specify the right margin for the PDF in millimeters (mm).

options.name: --settings-margin-bottom
options.description: Specify the bottom margin for the PDF in millimeters (mm).

options.name: --settings-margin-left
options.description: Specify the left margin for the PDF in millimeters (mm).

options.name: --settings-print-background
options.description: Specifies whether to print the background graphics and colors in the PDF. Set to "1" to include backgrounds or "0" to exclude them.

options.name: --settings-display-header-footer
options.description:
Specifies whether to display the header and footer in the PDF. Set to true to include the header and footer or false to exclude them.
Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --settings-custom-header
options.description: Specify custom HTML markup for the headerof the PDF. These properties should contain valid HTML markup, including any necessary CSS styles.

options.name: --settings-custom-footer
options.description: Specify custom HTML markup for the footer of the PDF. These properties should contain valid HTML markup, including any necessary CSS styles.

commands.name: create-pdf-from-url
commands.description:
Create a PDF from URL
- This endpoint creates a PDF file from a URL

options.name: --export-type
options.description:
- Either `file` or `json`(Default).
- The option `json` returns a JSON object, and the output PDF is stored on a CDN. Use this with the parameter `expiration`
- The option `file` returns binary data of the generated PDF(Secure and completely private) and the response HTTP header Content-Disposition is set to attachment.

options.name: --expiration
options.description:
- Expiration of the generated PDF in minutes(default to `0`, store permanently)
- Use `0` to store on cdn permanently
- Or use the range between `1` minute and `10080` minutes(7 days) to specify the expiration of the generated PDF

options.name: --output-format
options.description:
Specifies the desired output format. Options are `pdf` (default), `html`, `png`, or `jpeg`.
- By default, a PDF is generated.
- To return HTML instead, set `output_format=html`; the response will include a `download_url` field pointing to the HTML.
- To produce an image, set `output_format=png` or `output_format=jpeg`.

options.name: --filename
options.description: - Default to UUID (e.g 0c93bd9e-9ebb-4634-a70f-de9131848416.pdf). Use this to specify custom file name, it should end with `.pdf`

options.name: --direct-download
options.description: - ContentDisposition set to attachment. 1=true, 0=false. Default to '0'

options.name: --cloud-storage
options.description: - Upload the generated PDFs/images to our storage CDN, default to `1`. If you have configured `Post Action` to upload the PDFs/Images to your own S3, please set it to `0`.

options.name: --generation-delay
options.description: Delay in milliseconds before PDF/image generation

options.name: --image-resample-res
options.description: - We embed the original images by default, meaning large PDF file sizes. Specifying the option 'image_resample_res' helps reduce the PDF file size by downsampling the images of the current PDF to a resolution(in DPI). Common values are 72, 96, 150, 300 and 600.

options.name: --resize-images
options.description:
- Preprocess images or re-size images in the PDF, either `1`=true or `0`=false. Default to '0'
- If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the `resize_max_width`, `resize_max_height` in pixels.
- Images to be resized need to satisfy the following conditions:
- The images with the content-type `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg` or `image/png`
- The image URLs with the extension `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png`

options.name: --resize-max-width
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum width of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-max-height
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the maximum height of the image in pixels. Default to '1000'

options.name: --resize-format
options.description: - If `resize_images` is set to `1`, specify the format of the image. Either `jpeg` or `png`

options.name: --postaction-s3-filekey
options.description:
- This is to specify the file name for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2/Azure Storage)`.
- Please do not specify the file extension
- Please make sure the file name is unique
- You might use slash (/) as the folder delimiter
- It's default to transaction_ref

options.name: --postaction-s3-bucket
options.description: - This is to overwrite the AWS Bucket for `Post Action(AWS S3/Cloudflare R2 Storage)` or the container for `Post Action(Azure Storage)`.

options.name: --postaction-enabled
options.description:
- This setting enables the Post Actions.
- Acceptable values: `0` (disabled) or `1` (enabled; default).
- It is enabled by default. However, if you have enabled BYOS and do not upload the generated PDF/image of this request to your own storage, please set this to `0`.

options.name: --meta
options.description: - Specify an external reference ID for your own reference. It appears in the `list-objects` API.

options.name: --async
options.description:
- Either `1` or `0`(Default).  `0` is synchronous call(default), `1` is asynchronous call
- To generate PDF asynchronously, set the value to `1` and the API call returns immediately. Once the PDF document is generated, we will make a HTTP/HTTPS GET to your URL(webhook_url) and will retry for 3 times before giving up.
- If `async` is set to `1`, then `webhook_url` is mandatory

options.name: --webhook-url
options.description:
- It is the URL of your webhook URL, it starts with http:// or https:// and has to be urlencoded.
- If `async` is set to `1`, then you have to specify the `webhook_url`.
#### Format of Webhook callback
Once the PDF is generated, we will initiate a HTTP/HTTPS GET call to the following URL:
https://`[yourwebserver.com]`?&primary_url=`[primary_url]`&transaction_ref=`[transaction_ref]`&status=`[status]`&message=`[message]`
- `[yourwebserver.com]`: The web services to handle the callback, which is the `webhook_url`
- `[primary_url]`: The URL to the PDF document
- `[transaction_ref]`: The transaction reference number
- `[status]` : Status of the transaction, either `success` or `error`
- `[message]` : Status message
***The following is a sample webhook call back to your server***
https://yourwebserver.com?&primary_url=https%3A%2F%2Fpub-cdn.apitemplate.io%2F2021%2F06%2Fb692183d-46d7-3213-891a-460a5814ad3f.pdf&transaction_ref=b692183d-46d7-3213-891a-460a5814ad3f&status=success

options.name: --webhook-method
options.description: - The HTTP method of the webhook, either `POST` or `GET`. Default to `GET`
